slides.title: ~Filter~ like Excel
tip: Text goes in single quotes in SQL. 'Pune', not "Pune".

rows.name: Filter one city
rows.formula: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE city = 'Pune';
rows.result: 1 1 1 1 1 2024-01-10 500 5 Delivered West Pune, 2 2 1 1 3 2024-01-22 900 2 Delivered West Pune, 6 6 4 4 3 2024-03-09 450 1 Delivered West Pune, ...

rows.name: Number filter: above 1,000
rows.formula: SELECT order_id, amount FROM orders WHERE amount > 1000;

rows.name: Filter two values
rows.formula: SELECT order_id, city FROM orders WHERE city IN ('Pune', 'Kanpur');

rows.name: Text contains 'mail'
rows.formula: SELECT name, email FROM customers WHERE email LIKE '%mail%';
rows.result: Amit amit@mail.com, Divya divya@mail.com, Rahul rahul@mail.com, ...

rows.name: Filter blanks
rows.formula: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE phone IS NULL;

rows.name: Sort largest to smallest
rows.formula: SELECT order_id, amount FROM orders ORDER BY amount DESC;

slides.data: Practice tables (example): orders (8 orders, Pune, Indore, Kanpur), customers (5), employees (8 staff, some phones blank).

slides.title: Your ~formulas~, in SQL
tip: COUNT(*) counts rows. COUNT(phone) skips the blanks.

rows.name: SUM of a column
rows.formula: SELECT SUM(amount) FROM orders;

rows.name: COUNTIF status = Delivered
rows.formula: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE status = 'Delivered';

rows.name: SUMIF by city
rows.formula: SELECT city, SUM(amount) FROM orders GROUP BY city;

rows.name: AVERAGEIF by dept
rows.formula: SELECT dept, ROUND(AVG(salary)) FROM employees GROUP BY dept;

rows.name: MAX and MIN together
rows.formula: SELECT MAX(salary), MIN(salary) FROM employees;

rows.name: COUNTA vs COUNT
rows.formula: SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(phone) FROM employees;

slides.title: ~Pivot~ tables, in SQL
tip: WHERE filters rows before grouping. HAVING filters the groups after.

rows.name: Pivot: city x total and count
rows.formula: SELECT city, COUNT(*), SUM(amount) FROM orders GROUP BY city;

rows.name: Pivot with a report filter
rows.formula: SELECT region, SUM(amount) FROM orders WHERE status = 'Delivered' GROUP BY region;

rows.name: Value filter: totals above 3,000
rows.formula: SELECT city, SUM(amount) FROM orders GROUP BY city HAVING SUM(amount) > 3000;

rows.name: Top 2 cities by sales
rows.formula: SELECT city, SUM(amount) AS total FROM orders GROUP BY city ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 2;

rows.name: Remove duplicates
rows.formula: SELECT DISTINCT city FROM orders;

rows.name: Count unique customers
rows.formula: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) FROM orders;

slides.title: ~VLOOKUP~ and IF, in SQL
tip: LEFT JOIN keeps every order, like VLOOKUP. Missing matches show NULL, not #N/A.

rows.name: VLOOKUP customer name
rows.formula: SELECT o.order_id, c.name FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id;

rows.name: VLOOKUP that keeps missing
rows.formula: SELECT c.name, o.order_id FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_id IS NULL;

rows.name: IF: label big orders
rows.formula: SELECT order_id, CASE WHEN amount >= 1000 THEN 'Big' ELSE 'Small' END FROM orders;

rows.name: IFERROR for blanks
rows.formula: SELECT name, COALESCE(phone, 'Not given') FROM employees;

rows.name: Text: UPPER and LENGTH
rows.formula: SELECT UPPER(city), LENGTH(city) FROM customers;

rows.name: Month from a date
rows.formula: SELECT order_id, strftime('%m', order_date) FROM orders;
